title: Polish Past Tense: Endings, Gender and Irregular Verbs
excerpt: The Polish past tense explained for beginners: -łem/-łam endings, gender, the -li/-ły plural, irregular verbs, aspect and practice with answers.
metaDescription: The Polish past tense explained for beginners: -łem/-łam endings, gender, the -li/-ły plural, irregular verbs, aspect and practice with answers.
summary: Polish has one everyday past tense, built by dropping -ć from the infinitive and adding -ł- plus a personal ending.
Past forms change for gender: a man says byłem, a woman says byłam, and plural groups split into -li (at least one man) and -ły (everyone else).
Verbs in -eć swap e for a before ł (miał) but keep e in -li forms (mieli), while iść, jeść and móc have irregular past stems.
Aspect still matters in the past: robiłem describes a process, zrobiłem a finished result.
